items.title: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy

items.title: Deepfake detection by human crowds, machines, and machine-informed crowds

judge.evidence_empirical: In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.evidence_topic: The recent emergence of machine-manipulated media raises an important societal question: How can we know whether a video that we watch is real or fake? In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.reason: O achado descreve com precisão o que o resumo relata: similaridade de acurácia entre humanos e modelo, tipos de erros diferentes e o efeito negativo de previsões incorretas do modelo no desempenho dos participantes.

items.title: Fooled twice: People cannot detect deepfakes but think they can

judge.evidence_empirical: In a pre-registered behavioral experiment ( N = 210), we show that (a) people cannot reliably detect deepfakes
judge.evidence_topic: Hyper-realistic manipulation of audio-visual content, i.e., deepfakes, presents a new challenge for establishing veracity of online content.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a detecção humana de deepfakes, dentro do recorte (não político, não saúde), usando experimento com N=210, método extraído compatível, e o achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: Speech deepfakes are artificial voices generated by machine learning models. ... We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.reason: O achado principal relatado (detecção correta em cerca de 73%, sem diferença entre idiomas, indicando detecção não confiável) é sustentado integralmente pelo resumo, que afirma: "Listeners only correctly spotted the deepfakes 73% of the time, and there was no difference in detectability between the two languages. ... detection capability is unreliable."

items.title: AI Hyperrealism: Why AI Faces Are Perceived as More Real Than Human Ones

judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults) ... In Experiment 2 ( N = 610 adults)
judge.evidence_topic: White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces—a phenomenon we term AI hyperrealism.
judge.reason: O resumo descreve dois experimentos com participantes humanos e relata exatamente o achado extraído: rostos brancos de IA foram julgados como humanos com mais frequência do que rostos humanos reais, e os que mais erravam eram os mais confiantes (efeito Dunning-Kruger).

items.title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

judge.evidence_empirical: We tested these questions using AI-generated voices generated with and without a specific human counterpart (i.e., voice clones, and voices generated from the latent space of a large voice model). We find that voice clones can sound as real as human voices, making it difficult for listeners to distinguish between them.
judge.evidence_topic: We investigated the extent to which AI-generated voices sound real to human listeners, and whether listeners can accurately distinguish between human and AI-generated voices.
judge.reason: O resumo indica claramente um experimento com ouvintes humanos julgando realismo e discriminando vozes, o que confere com o estudo empírico com participantes humanos. O achado principal extraído reflete exatamente o que o resumo afirma: clones de voz soam tão reais quanto vozes humanas, dificultando a distinção, mas sem efeito de hiper-realismo.

items.title: Cortical-striatal brain network distinguishes deepfake from real speaker identity

judge.evidence_empirical: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.
judge.reason: Humans can thus be partly tricked by deepfakes, but the neurocognitive mechanisms identified during deepfake processing open windows for strengthening human resilience to fake information. On the brain level, univariate and multivariate analyses consistently reveal a central cortico-striatal network that decoded the vocal acoustic pattern and deepfake-level (auditory cortex), as well as natural speaker identities (nucleus accumbens).

items.title: The Effect of Deepfake Video on News Credibility and Corrective Influence of Cost-Based Knowledge about Deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: This study conducted an experiment (N = 230)
judge.evidence_topic: This study conducted an experiment (N = 230) that tested (1) how a news article using deepfake video (vs. real video) affects news credibility and viral behavioral intentions and (2) whether, based on signaling theory, obtaining knowledge about the low cost of producing deepfakes reduces the impact of deepfake news.
judge.reason: O achado extraído é suportado pelo resumo: pessoas com atitudes congruentes acreditam e compartilham deepfake news tanto quanto real video news, e informar sobre o baixo custo dos deepfakes reduz a credibilidade para essas pessoas.
